summary: Bahia state's facial recognition pilot in Salvador was reported to misidentify people, including a young Black man who was followed across 15 metro stations and then stopped by police. The state kept expanding the system despite a low hit rate.
technical_summary: Police facial recognition cameras matched passing faces against a database of wanted people and sent alerts to officers. Reporting said only 3.6% of 903 alerts at a 2019 festival led to arrest warrants. The failure mechanism is face-matching error generating false alerts that led to a wrongful police stop. The description also says the system disproportionately targeted Black and poor people; the excerpt supports this only as a pattern of cases.

summary: A license-plate reader alert led Jackson Township police in Ohio to briefly stop a driver whose car matched an old missing-juvenile hot-list entry. The juvenile had already been found, and a federal court later addressed the vendor's role in the stale record.
technical_summary: Flock Safety license-plate reader cameras flagged vehicles against NCIC hot-list data. The alert matched a car to an entry from a closed investigation, and officers stopped the driver. The failure is a stale law-enforcement record feeding an automated match. The vendor was sued, but a federal court held that it did not create the stale entry.

The core mechanism is conventional security failure rather than an AI system flaw.
